local_facts.claim: NWS Twin Cities reports current winter averages of 19 days with lows at or below 0°F and 55 days with highs at or below 32°F. In Eden Prairie, garage-door hardware can therefore face repeated deeply cold starts rather than one isolated storm day.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Repeated cold makes old lubricant sluggish, contracts steel hardware, and can freeze a weather seal to the slab. Those conditions expose worn springs, bearings, rollers, and marginal balance, so the repair checks the whole moving system rather than increasing opener force.
local_facts.title: Deep cold is a season-long operating condition

local_facts.claim: Minnesota's Residential Energy Code identifies garages as unconditioned space for its duct-insulation rules and requires a nonconditioned space altered to become conditioned to comply fully with the code.
local_facts.why_it_matters: An insulated replacement door or a repaired perimeter seal can improve comfort and protect equipment, but that does not itself make an attached garage part of the conditioned home. A garage conversion or duct change should be considered separately from ordinary door repair.
local_facts.title: A garage is not automatically conditioned living space

local_facts.claim: Eden Prairie accepts building permit applications through its paperless ePermits portal. The City says permits are required for work regulated by the Minnesota State Building Code, including structural alterations or repairs to permanent weather-resistive surfaces, and all permitted work is subject to inspection.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Spring, cable, roller, and opener repairs are different from changing structural framing or modifying a garage opening. When a door project reaches that larger scope, permit confirmation belongs in the plan before material is ordered.
local_facts.title: Structural changes need an Eden Prairie permit check

anchors.detail: The city's lowest valuation tier. Work valued between $2,001 and $25,000 is $105.25 for the first $2,000 plus $19.75 per additional $1,000, with plan checking at 65 percent and reinspection at $50.00 per hour.

anchors.label: Minnesota construction surcharge on a fixed-fee permit
anchors.detail: State surcharge collected by the city on every permit for construction, addition or alteration: one-half mill of the permit fee or one dollar on fixed-fee permits, and 0.0005 of valuation on valuation-based permits.
